title: Optimized 4C-seq Protocol for RAW264.7 Macrophage Cell Line
author: Huang, Wang, et al.
materials: The following steps are the first restricted enzyme digestion (1st RE digestion) (Figure 2D).16.Carefully remove the supernatant and resuspend the cell nuclei with 440 μL distilled water (DNase and RNase free).17.Add 60 μL 10× digestion buffer and 15 μL of 10% SDS.18.Incubate the samples in a thermomixer at 37°C with 900 rpm shaking for 1 h.19.Add additional 75 μL of 20% Triton X-100 into each sample. Pipet up and down to mix all the samples.20.Incubate the samples in a thermomixer at 37°C with 900 rpm shaking for another 1 h.21.Take 5 μL of each sample as “undigested control”. Save the samples in −20°C.22.Add 200 U of first restricted enzyme (1st RE) (in this case, we use DpnII.) to each sample. Pipet up and down to mix all the samples.23.Incubate all the samples in thermomixer at 37°C with 900 rpm shaking for another 4 h.24.Add additional 200 U first restricted enzyme (DpnII) in each sample and incubate overnight at 37°C with 900 rpm shaking.25.Take 5 μL of digestion sample from each sample. Process the digestion efficiency quality control.26.Add 40 μL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) into the “undigested controls” and “digestion samples”.27.Add 5 μL protease K (10 mg/mL) into each sample and incubate at 65°C at least 2 h.28.Add 8 μL DNA loading buffer into each sample and take 10 μL each sample for the DNA agarose gel (1%) as quality control (example gel in Figure 3A). Use 3 μL of 1 kb DNA ladder to mark the DNA fragments. Keep the rest of samples in −20°C for further usage.Figure 3Quality control for 4C-seq(A) An example gel picture of the products from the 4C protocol.(B) TapeStation test for the quality control of the DNA distribution of the 4C-seq library.29.If the digestion is good, the first ligation can be proceeded. Otherwise, repeat the digestion by adding additional 200 U of first enzyme (DpnII) and incubate overnight at 37°C with 900 rpm shaking.CRITICAL: The ideal digestion efficiencies are somewhat different according to the enzyme selection, but the proportion of the digestion fragments should be less than 10 kb compared to the undigestion control and the distribution of the fragments are dispersed between 200 bp to 3 kb (example gel in Figure 3A).

The following steps are the first ligation (Figure 2E).30.Heat-inactivate the first enzyme (DpnII) using 65°C for 20 min and cold down the samples on ice.31.Transfer the samples into 50 mL tubes and add 700 μL 10× T4 ligation buffer and distilled water (DNase and RNase free) up to 7 mL.32.Add 10 μL T4 ligase (4000 NEB units or equal to 20 Welss Units) to each sample and pipet up and down to mix all the samples.33.Incubate all the samples at room temperature with gentle shaking overnight.34.The next day, take 50 μL of each ligation sample and add 5 μL protease K (10 mg/mL) and incubate for at least 2 h at 65°C.35.Run a DNA agarose gel (1%) as quality control to check the 1st ligation efficiency with the previous digestion samples (step 28) (example gel in Figure 3A).36.If the ligation quality is satisfied, process the reverse-crosslinking by adding 30 μL protease K (10 mg/mL) and incubating all the samples at 65°C overnight. Otherwise add 50 μL additional ATP (10 mM) to each sample and incubate them overnight at room temperature with gentle shaking (repeat 33–35 for re-ligation).CRITICAL: When doing the ligation, it is better to avoid the cell pellets formation at the bottom, which will affect the ligation efficiency. The shaking rate should be less than 50 rpm/min.

The following steps are the second enzyme digestion (2nd RE digestion) (Figure 2F).49.Add 50 μL 10× second digestion buffer (in our case we used NlaIII) and 100 U NlaIII. Pipet up and down to mix all samples.50.Incubate all samples in a thermomixer at 37°C overnight with 900 rpm shaking.51.Take 5 μL each sample and dilute it in 45 μL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0). Add 10 μL DNA loading buffer and take 10 μL of samples to run a DNA agarose gel (1%) as quality control to check the 2nd digestion efficiency with the previous first ligation samples. Save the rest of samples with previous digestion and ligation samples for future usage.

The following steps are the second ligation (Figure 2G).52.Heat-inactivate the second digestion enzyme using 65°C for 20 min and cold down the samples on ice.53.Transfer all samples to 50 mL tubes and add 700 μL T4 ligation buffer (10×) and distilled water (DNase and RNase free) up to 7 mL.54.Add 10 μL T4 ligase (4000 NEB units or equal to 20 Welss units) to each sample and pipet up and down to mix all the samples.55.Incubate all the samples at room temperature without shaking.56.Run a DNA agarose gel (1%) as quality control to check the 2nd ligation efficiency with the previous digestion samples (example gel in Figure 3A).

steps.title: Wash and lyse cells
steps.instruction: Prepare 10 million RAW264.7 cells for 4C by washing, lysing and pelleting nuclei.

substeps.instruction: Wash cells once with 1 mL cold DPBS containing protease inhibitors.
Spin at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL lysis buffer (with protease inhibitors); pipet up/down until the pellet is disrupted.
Keep tubes on ice for 10 min.
Centrifuge at 1,000 × g for 5 min at 4 °C and discard supernatant.

steps.title: First restriction digestion (DpnII)
steps.instruction: Digest nuclei with DpnII to generate the first 3C fragments.

substeps.instruction: Remove supernatant and resuspend nuclei in 440 µL DNase/RNase‑free water.
Add 60 µL 10× DpnII digestion buffer and 15 µL 10 % SDS; mix.
Incubate at 37 °C, 900 rpm shaking for 1 h.
Add 75 µL 20 % Triton X‑100; mix.
Incubate at 37 °C, 900 rpm shaking for another 1 h.
Aliquot 5 µL as “undigested control” and store at –20 °C.
Add 200 U DpnII (first RE) to each sample; mix.
Incubate at 37 °C, 900 rpm shaking for 4 h.
Add an additional 200 U DpnII and incubate overnight at 37 °C, 900 rpm shaking.
Take 5 µL of the digestion mixture for QC.
Add 40 µL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) to both undigested controls and digestion samples.
Add 5 µL proteinase K (10 mg/mL) and incubate at 65 °C for at least 2 h.
Add 8 µL DNA loading buffer, load 10 µL on a 1 % agarose gel with 3 µL 1 kb ladder; keep remaining sample at –20 °C.
If digestion fragments are >10 kb or distribution is not 200 bp–3 kb, repeat digestion by adding another 200 U DpnII and incubate overnight.

steps.title: First ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate the DpnII‑digested fragments to create the first 3C library.

substeps.instruction: Heat‑inactivate DpnII at 65 °C for 20 min; place on ice.
Transfer each sample to a 50 mL tube and add 700 µL 10× T4 ligation buffer and DNase/RNase‑free water up to 7 mL total.
Add 10 µL T4 DNA ligase (4000 NEB U ≈ 20 Welch U); mix gently.
Incubate at room temperature with gentle shaking (≤50 rpm) overnight.
Next day, take 50 µL ligation sample, add 5 µL proteinase K (10 mg/mL) and incubate at 65 °C for ≥2 h.
Run a 1 % agarose gel (as in step 28) to assess ligation efficiency.
If ligation is satisfactory, add 30 µL proteinase K (10 mg/mL) and incubate at 65 °C overnight for reverse‑crosslinking.
If not satisfactory, add 50 µL 10 mM ATP, incubate overnight at room temperature with gentle shaking, then repeat ligation QC.

steps.title: First DNA purification
steps.instruction: Purify the 3C DNA after the first ligation and reverse‑crosslinking.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µL RNase A (10 mg/mL) to each sample; incubate 30 min at 37 °C water bath.
Add 7 mL phenol–chloroform; vortex vigorously for 5 min.
Centrifuge 20 min at 2,000 × g at room temperature.
Transfer the upper aqueous phase to a new 50 mL tube.
Add 7 mL DNase/RNase‑free water, 1.5 mL 2 M NaAc (pH 5.6), 10 µL glycogen (20 mg/mL) and 35 mL 100 % ethanol; mix.
Freeze at –80 °C for at least 1 h (ensure complete freezing).
Centrifuge 20 min at 2,000 × g at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 10 mL cold (–20 °C) 70 % ethanol; centrifuge 20 min at 2,000 × g at 4 °C.
Discard supernatant and air‑dry pellet at room temperature.
Resuspend pellet in 450 µL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0); transfer to a 1.5 mL tube (3C DNA template).
Measure DNA concentration with Qubit.
Aliquot 5 µL DNA + 45 µL 10 mM Tris; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Safe stop point after first purification
steps.instruction: Store the 3C DNA template at –20 °C; it remains stable for months.

steps.title: Second restriction digestion (NlaIII)
steps.instruction: Digest the first‑ligated 3C DNA with NlaIII to generate fragments for circularization.

substeps.instruction: Add 50 µL 10× NlaIII second‑digestion buffer and 100 U NlaIII to each sample; mix.
Incubate at 37 °C, 900 rpm shaking overnight.
Take 5 µL of each sample, dilute in 45 µL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0), add 10 µL DNA loading buffer, and run a 1 % agarose gel to assess digestion efficiency.
Retain the remaining sample for the second ligation.

steps.title: Second ligation
steps.instruction: Ligate the NlaIII‑digested fragments to generate circular DNA suitable for 4C‑PCR.

substeps.instruction: Heat‑inactivate NlaIII at 65 °C for 20 min; chill on ice.
Transfer samples to 50 mL tubes, add 700 µL 10× T4 ligation buffer and DNase/RNase‑free water up to 7 mL.
Add 10 µL T4 DNA ligase (4000 NEB U ≈ 20 Welch U); mix.
Incubate at room temperature without shaking.
Run a 1 % agarose gel to verify second‑ligation efficiency.

steps.title: Second DNA purification
steps.instruction: Purify the circular 4C template after the second ligation.

substeps.instruction: Add 7 mL DNase/RNase‑free water, 1.5 mL 2 M NaAc (pH 5.6), 10 µL glycogen (10 mg/mL) and 35 mL 100 % ethanol; mix.
Freeze at –80 °C for at least 1 h.
Centrifuge 20 min at 2,000 × g at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Wash pellet with 10 mL cold (–20 °C) 70 % ethanol; centrifuge 20 min at 2,000 × g at 4 °C.
Air‑dry pellet at room temperature.
Resuspend in 400 µL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0) and transfer to a 1.5 mL tube.
Purify using the QIAquick PCR purification kit (four columns per sample); elute each column with 80 µL 10 mM Tris (pH 8.0).
Combine the four eluates (~320 µL total).
Measure DNA concentration with Qubit or NanoDrop; typical 4C template concentration is 50–100 ng/µL.
Aliquot 5 µL DNA + 45 µL 10 mM Tris; store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Safe stop point after second purification
steps.instruction: Store the purified 4C template DNA at –20 °C; it can be kept for months.

steps.title: DNA repair and template preparation (ThruPLEX)
steps.instruction: Prepare the 4C‑PCR products for library construction using the Takara ThruPLEX DNA‑Seq kit (or equivalent).

substeps.instruction: Mix 10 µL 4C‑PCR product with 2 µL template‑preparation buffer and 1 µL preparation enzyme; pipet to mix.
Place in a PCR thermocycler and incubate 25 °C for 25 min then 55 °C for 20 min.
Total input DNA amount will determine the number of PCR cycles in later steps; follow the kit’s recommendations.

steps.title: Stem‑loop adapter assembly and library synthesis
steps.instruction: Add adapters and synthesize the library.

substeps.instruction: Add 1 µL library‑synthesis buffer and 1 µL library‑synthesis enzyme to the repaired DNA.
Incubate at 22 °C for 40 min.

steps.title: Library amplification with index primers
steps.instruction: Amplify the library and introduce sample‑specific indexes.

substeps.instruction: Add 25 µL library‑amplification buffer, 4 µL distilled water and 1 µL library‑amplification enzyme.
Add the appropriate Takara ThruPLEX index primer.
Run the following PCR program:
• 72 °C 3 min (extension)
• 85 °C 2 min (cleavage)
• 98 °C 2 min (denaturation)
• 98 °C 20 s, 67 °C 20 s, 72 °C 40 s (first cycle)
• 98 °C 20 s then 5–16 cycles (number of cycles depends on starting DNA; 5–8 cycles are typical for 4C‑seq).
• Hold at 4 °C.
Take 1 µL of the PCR product and measure DNA concentration with Qubit.
If concentration is 10–30 ng/µL, proceed; if <5 ng/µL, add two additional cycles. Avoid over‑amplification.

steps.title: Library purification with AMPure beads
steps.instruction: Perform double‑size selection to remove primer dimers and large fragments.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 50 µL library into a 96‑well plate.
Add 25 µL AMPure beads (0.5×); mix by pipetting at least ten times.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Place plate on a 96‑well magnetic stand for 5 min.
Transfer the supernatant (contains fragments <~300 bp) to a new well (removes large fragments).
Add 60 µL AMPure beads (1.2×) to the transferred supernatant; mix.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic stand for 5 min.
Transfer the supernatant (now free of index primers) to a new well.
Wash the beads twice with 200 µL fresh 80 % ethanol (30 s each wash).
Air‑dry beads for 2–5 min at room temperature.
Add 35 µL distilled water to the beads; mix.
Incubate 5 min at room temperature.
Place on magnetic stand for 5 min and collect 32 µL supernatant into a 1.5 mL tube.
Measure DNA concentration with Qubit.
Assess library size distribution on a TapeStation; acceptable libraries show no primer dimers (<100 bp) and no large fragments.
If quality passes, pool indexed libraries at appropriate concentrations for sequencing.

steps.title: Sequencing preparation
steps.instruction: Pool the final 4C‑seq libraries and submit for Illumina sequencing.

substeps.instruction: Combine all indexed libraries in equimolar amounts.
Sequence using single‑read 50 bp or 75 bp reads; 1–5 million reads per sample are sufficient for downstream analysis.
